title: Panics-section and lock-poisoning expect() treatment is inconsistent
description:
Scoped to the panic-documentation points; the broader missing-docs sweep is persona-5s4b.78.

rust.md: functions that can panic need a `## Panics` section, but it "documents only caller-triggerable conditions — panics a caller at the item's visibility can cause while respecting its contract", and a poisoned mutex is the canonical case for a bare `.unwrap()` because `PoisonError` already explains itself.

Three sites in hire-core/src/trust_bundle.rs use `.expect("trust bundle lock poisoned")`: `upsert` (:50), `snapshot` (:58) and `get` (:69). The message adds nothing that `PoisonError`'s own Display does not already say, so per rust.md these should be plain `.unwrap()`. A poisoned lock here means another thread panicked while holding it — our bug, not the caller's — so it correctly gets no `## Panics` section either. Right now the three `.expect` strings imply a documented contract that is not documented anywhere.

hire-core/src/signer.rs:98-100 is the opposite case and is handled correctly:

    .expect("system clock before epoch")

That one states an invariant the `Err` does not carry, so `.expect` is right — but `sign_jwt_svid` has no `## Panics` section saying a pre-epoch clock aborts issuance. It is environment-triggerable rather than argument-triggerable, so it belongs in the doc as a "may panic if".

Fix: drop the three `.expect` messages in trust_bundle.rs to `.unwrap()`, and add a `## Panics` line to `sign_jwt_svid`.
